title: A high-dilution TESS eclipse fit of TYC 9179-1083-1 improves the published shape fit
abstract: We test large third-light fractions against published TESS eclipse profiles of TYC 9179-1083-1. A two-sphere fit at TESS third-light fraction 0.7849 gives chi-square 2246.73, compared with 3538.39 for the published zero-light fit with the same 15 free shape parameters. Its inclination change from 2018 to 2026 is 0.817 degrees instead of 0.376 degrees. Exposure averaging gives chi-square 2243.41. Two radius-ratio starts recover the same bright solution; larger-radius starts find a worse local minimum. Free physical quadratic limb darkening gives chi-square 2220.26 for the bright example. These results show that large dilution can fit the eclipse shapes and bring the shape drift closer to the earlier timing prediction of about 0.73 degrees. The bright shape has different eccentricity and periastron angles from the geometry used in the timing and Gaia fits. It is not a joint physical orbit. Gaia G-band and TESS light fractions also need not agree. We preserve code, input hashes, local search states, negative results, figures and reproduction instructions. The tests use published season means, inherit their errors and use local searches. They do not measure the tertiary light or identify a compact object.

display.caption: Local shape fits across tested TESS third-light fractions. The searches can reach different geometry branches. The dashed line marks the approximate prior timing-model inclination change. These are conditional fits, not light-fraction confidence limits.
Published season means and fitted eclipse profiles at zero and 0.7849 TESS third-light fraction. Both fits use the same number of shape parameters.

citations.reason: We reuse the published measurements and model. A high-dilution geometry improves the source shape fit and changes its inferred inclination and periastron angles.

We test the large numerical light fractions of the astrometric branches in the TESS band. We find an explicit good shape fit, but do not establish a common physical orbit or equal fractions across bands.
